title: twentyhq/twenty — The open alternative to Salesforce, designed for AI.
content:
Website · Documentation · Roadmap · Discord · Figma
Twenty gives technical teams the building blocks for a custom CRM that meets complex business needs and quickly adapts as the business evolves. Twenty is the CRM you build, ship, and version like the rest of your stack.
Learn more about why we built Twenty
The fastest way to get started. Sign up at twenty.com and spin up a workspace in under a minute, with no infrastructure to manage and always up to date.
Scaffold a new app with the Twenty CLI:
npx create-twenty-app my-app
Define objects, fields, and views as code:
import { defineObject, FieldType } from 'twenty-sdk/define';
export default defineObject({
  nameSingular: 'deal',
  namePlural: 'deals',
  labelSingular: 'Deal',
  labelPlural: 'Deals',
  fields: [
    { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: FieldType.TEXT },
    { name: 'amount', label: 'Amount', type: FieldType.CURRENCY },
    { name: 'closeDate', label: 'Close Date', type: FieldType.DATE_TIME },
  ],
});
Then ship it to your workspace:
npx twenty app:publish --private
See the app development guide for objects, views, agents, and logic functions.
Run Twenty on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, or contribute locally via the local setup guide.
Twenty gives you the building blocks of a modern CRM (objects, views, workflows, and agents) and lets you extend them as code. Here's a tour of what's in the box.
Want to go deeper? Read the User Guide for product walkthroughs, or the Documentation for developer reference.
- TypeScript
- Nx
- NestJS, with BullMQ, PostgreSQL, Redis
- React, with Jotai, Linaria and Lingui
Thanks to these amazing services that we use and recommend for code review (Greptile), catching bugs (Sentry) and translating (Crowdin).

report.summary: Twenty is an open-source, AI-ready CRM alternative to Salesforce that lets developers build, ship, and version CRM apps as code.
report.background: Traditional CRM platforms like Salesforce are powerful but often rigid, expensive, and difficult for technical teams to customize beyond built-in limits. Twenty addresses this by offering an open-source alternative that treats the CRM as part of the modern software stack. The project combines a TypeScript-based framework with a React frontend, NestJS backend, and PostgreSQL for storage, giving developers the ability to define objects, fields, and views as code. This code-first approach means the CRM can be version-controlled, tested, and deployed like any other application. The project has gained traction for its flexibility, letting teams self-host via Docker Compose or quickly spin up a managed workspace. As AI becomes more integrated into business workflows, Twenty positions itself as an AI-ready foundation, supporting agents and logic functions out of the box.
key_points: Twenty is a true open-source alternative to Salesforce, giving technical teams full ownership over their CRM layer without vendor lock-in. Instead of clicking through admin panels, developers define data models in TypeScript and treat the CRM as infrastructure they can control and extend.

The platform uses a code-first approach: objects, fields, views, and logic functions are declared as TypeScript modules using the Twenty SDK. Teams can scaffold a new app with `create-twenty-app`, publish changes via the CLI, and keep everything in version control.

Deployment is flexible. Users can create a managed workspace on twenty.com in under a minute, or self-host with Docker Compose on their own infrastructure. This suits startups needing speed as well as enterprises with strict data residency or compliance requirements.

The stack is modern and familiar: TypeScript, Nx, NestJS, BullMQ, PostgreSQL, Redis, and React with Jotai. This lowers the learning curve for full-stack developers and makes it easier to integrate with existing engineering workflows and observability tools.

Twenty explicitly designs for AI workflows, mentioning agents and custom logic functions as core building blocks. This positions it beyond a standard CRM—it aims to become a platform where AI can natively operate on business data like deals, contacts, and pipelines.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Twenty represents a shift toward open, programmable data platforms that AI agents can directly interact with. Developers benefit because they can version CRM logic, automate workflows with code, and extend the system without waiting for vendor features. Regular users gain a modern, fast interface and the ability to customize the CRM to match how their business actually runs, instead of adapting to rigid prebuilt modules. As enterprises look to reduce Salesforce licensing costs and integrate AI into operations, open-source AI-ready CRMs like Twenty could accelerate adoption, especially among technically savvy teams.
report.tools: To follow up, watch Twenty's official repos and SDK: the `create-twenty-app` CLI and `twenty-sdk` are the entry points for building on the platform. For self-hosting, use Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis. Developers can also explore the Nx build system and NestJS backend used under the hood, or join the Twenty Discord for community patterns and contributions.
